title: Direct Induction Proof Of Loomis Theorem
body_html:
Direct Induction Proof Of Loomis Theorem

For matrices $A$ and $B$ indexed by $I\times J$, with $B_{ij}>0$, prove the existence and uniqueness of $v\in\mathbb R$ and strategies $s\in\Delta(I)$, $t\in\Delta(J)$ such that $$ sA\ge v\,sB,\qquad At\le v\,Bt. $$ The proof proceeds by induction on $|I|+|J|$. The induction step introduces $$ \lambda_0=\sup\{\lambda:\exists s\in\Delta(I),\ sA\ge \lambda sB\} $$ and $$ \mu_0=\inf\{\mu:\exists t\in\Delta(J),\ At\le \mu Bt\}, $$ then rules out $\lambda_0<\mu_0$ by deleting a column or row and using the induction hypothesis on the smaller matrix pair.
proof_html:
The sets in the definitions of $\lambda_0$ and $\mu_0$ are nonempty and bounded because every entry of $B$ is strictly positive. Compactness of the simplices makes the extrema attained by some $s_0\in\Delta(I)$ and $t_0\in\Delta(J)$, and the definitions give $\lambda_0\le\mu_0$.

It remains to exclude $\lambda_0<\mu_0$. If all inequalities $s_0A\ge\lambda_0 s_0B$ and $At_0\le\mu_0Bt_0$ were equalities, then $$ s_0At_0=\lambda_0 s_0Bt_0 \quad\text{and}\quad s_0At_0=\mu_0 s_0Bt_0. $$ Since $s_0Bt_0>0$, this would force $\lambda_0=\mu_0$. Hence, when $\lambda_0<\mu_0$, at least one of the two systems has a strict inequality in some column or row.

Suppose first that $s_0A>\lambda_0s_0B$ in some column $j_0$. Delete that column and apply the induction hypothesis to the smaller pair. The smaller game has a Loomis level $v'$ with $v'\ge\mu_0>\lambda_0$: deleting a column makes the requirements on player $1$ weaker and therefore cannot lower the relevant guarantee below the old upper level. Let $s'$ be the inductive row strategy for the smaller pair. For sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, the convex combination $$ s_\alpha=\alpha s'+(1-\alpha)s_0 $$ still satisfies the strict $j_0$ inequality and satisfies $s_\alpha A\ge\lambda_0s_\alpha B$ on the remaining columns. The strictness in at least one column lets the level be raised above $\lambda_0$, contradicting the definition of $\lambda_0$.

The case with a strict row inequality for $t_0$ is dual. Delete that row, apply the induction hypothesis to the smaller pair, and mix the resulting column strategy with $t_0$ by a small amount. This lowers the admissible upper level below $\mu_0$, contradicting the definition of $\mu_0$. Therefore $\lambda_0=\mu_0$. Taking $v$ to be this common value and the attaining strategies $s_0,t_0$ gives the Loomis inequalities.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 2.8, Exercise 1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Direct induction proof of Loomis theorem, independent of von Neumann minimax.
